newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end mixed, S&Ps lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed mixed, with Standard & Poor 500s finishing slightly lower in uneventful, pre-holiday trade, traders said.
"There weren't too many traders in the pit to do too much damage," one S&P futures floor source said.
He said most of the day's trades were transacted in the first two hours of trade. Estimated volume for December was 65,000 contracts.
CME stock index futures will be closed on Thursday for the U.S. Thanksgiving day holiday, and trade will end at 1215 CST/1815 GMT on Friday.

While U.S. stock index futures remained open all day on Wednesday, an abbreviated session in the U.S. bond futures market contributed to the low liquidity in S&Ps, they said. U.S. bond futures will close at 1210 CST/1810 GMT on Friday.
However, the selloff in the U.S. bond market lingered in the S&P futures pit throughout the day, analysts and traders said.
Most of the U.S. economic reports released on Wednesday indicated that the pace of U.S. economic growth was stronger than average trade expectations.
Traders cited the U.S. October durable goods orders and the November Chicago purchasing managers index in particular for the bond market's breakdown.

Durable goods rose 0.1 percent in October, versus the average trade estimate of down two percent, while the Chicago purchasing managers index increased to 57.6 in November, compared to estimates of 55.1.
On Monday, the National Association of Purchasing Management index for November will be released.
While Nasdaq 100s and other stock index futures were higher, Nikkeis fell in sympathy with S&P 500s.

Traders also attributed declines in the Nikkei 225 futures to the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) "Tankan" business sentiment survey, traders said. The survey showed that Japan's companies remain wary about the future.
Heavy spreading was noted in S&P 500s and Nikkei futures, as traders rolled positions into March. The last trading day for December Nikkeis is Thursday, December 12.
While the last trading day for December S&Ps is three weeks away, traders noted aggressive spreading into March.
The spread between December and March S&Ps widened out to 7.10 points this afternoon.
Based on fair value, the premium between the two contracts should be about 6.50 points. At the beginning of November, the spread stood at 6.25 points, one floor analyst said.

At the end of pit trade, December S&P 500s fell 1.40 points to 755.95, New Composites lost 0.85 to 398.15, KBT Value Lines were up 0.80 to 682.20, Nikkei 225s declined 80.0 to 21,335, Midcap 400s were 0.60 higher at 256.75 and Nasdaq 100s jumped 7.95 to 833.60. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
